name: 74HC165 8-bit parallel-in shift register
description: 8-bit parallel-in / serial-out shift register (high-speed CMOS): SH/LD low loads inputs A-H at once, then each rising CLK edge shifts one bit out on QH (H first). Reads 8 switches with 3 GPIOs; chips daisy-chain through SER. Runs on 2-6 V, inputs and outputs swing rail to rail, 80 uA max quiescent. Sold as: Texas Instruments SN74HC165N (bare 16-pin DIP chip that plugs straight into a breadboard; also sold as 74HC165 DIP-16 by Nexperia/onsemi clones), pins numbered 1-16 anticlockwise from the notch.
eli5: Lets your board read eight buttons or switches using only three wires, by passing their on/off states along one at a time.

pins.name: SH/LD
pins.description: Pin 1: shift/load. Low = copy inputs A-H into the register; high = shift on CLK

pins.name: CLK
pins.description: Pin 2: clock input, each rising edge shifts the next bit onto QH (while SH/LD is high and CLK INH low)

pins.name: E
pins.description: Pin 3: parallel input E. Never leave it floating: a switch to VCC with a 10 kOhm pull-down to GND (pressed = 1)

pins.name: F
pins.description: Pin 4: parallel input F. Never leave it floating: a switch to VCC with a 10 kOhm pull-down to GND (pressed = 1)

pins.name: G
pins.description: Pin 5: parallel input G. Never leave it floating: a switch to VCC with a 10 kOhm pull-down to GND (pressed = 1)

pins.name: H
pins.description: Pin 6: parallel input H. Never leave it floating: a switch to VCC with a 10 kOhm pull-down to GND (pressed = 1)

pins.name: /QH
pins.description: Pin 7: complementary (inverted) serial output. Not needed: leave unconnected

pins.name: QH
pins.description: Pin 9: serial output, the last bit of the register (H first after a load). Swings to VCC, so run the chip from 3.3 V for a 3.3 V board

pins.name: SER
pins.description: Pin 10: serial input shifted in behind the data. Tie to GND for one chip (or to QH of the next chip in a chain); never floating

pins.name: A
pins.description: Pin 11: parallel input A. Never leave it floating: a switch to VCC with a 10 kOhm pull-down to GND (pressed = 1)

pins.name: B
pins.description: Pin 12: parallel input B. Never leave it floating: a switch to VCC with a 10 kOhm pull-down to GND (pressed = 1)

pins.name: C
pins.description: Pin 13: parallel input C. Never leave it floating: a switch to VCC with a 10 kOhm pull-down to GND (pressed = 1)

pins.name: D
pins.description: Pin 14: parallel input D. Never leave it floating: a switch to VCC with a 10 kOhm pull-down to GND (pressed = 1)

pins.name: CLK INH
pins.description: Pin 15: clock inhibit, high = CLK ignored. Tie to GND (or drive it low from a GPIO)

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Pin 16: supply 2-6 V (use 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico). 0.1 uF to GND close to the pin

buildNotes: Pin 1 (SH/LD) is next to the notch/dot; pins count anticlockwise seen from the top, so VCC (pin 16) is opposite pin 1 and GND is pin 8.
Power it from 3.3 V when the board is an ESP32 or Pico: QH swings to VCC, and 5 V on a GPIO can damage it.
Tie CLK INH (pin 15) and SER (pin 10) to GND for a single chip. CMOS inputs must never float (datasheet note on recommended operating conditions).
Every input A-H needs a defined level: wire each switch from the input to VCC with a 10 kOhm pull-down to GND (pressed = 1), or switch to GND with a 10 kOhm pull-up (pressed = 0).
Read sequence: pulse SH/LD low then high, read QH (that is H), then for each of the remaining bits pulse CLK high and read QH again. 8 bits: H, G, F, E, D, C, B, A.
Chain more chips by wiring QH of the far chip into SER of the near one and sharing SH/LD and CLK; then clock 16, 24... bits.
Put a 0.1 uF capacitor between VCC (pin 16) and GND (pin 8), close to the chip.

driver.code:
# MicroPython driver for the 74HC165 8-bit parallel-in / serial-out shift register
# (TI SN74HC165, datasheet SCLS116H).
#
# How the chip works (datasheet section 8):
#   - SH/LD low copies the eight parallel inputs A..H into the register at once
#     (CLK, CLK INH and SER are ignored while SH/LD is low).
#   - With SH/LD high and CLK INH low, every rising edge of CLK shifts the register
#     one place toward QH; SER feeds the empty end (H is on QH first, A last).
#   - QH (pin 9) shows the bit at the end of the register; /QH (pin 7) is its inverse.
# Daisy-chain: QH of chip 2 -> SER of chip 1, so after 8 clocks chip 2's bits follow.
# All datasheet timings are tens of ns; MicroPython pin toggles take microseconds,
# so no extra delays are needed.

from machine import Pin


class HC165:
    def __init__(self, load, clock, data, clk_inh=None, chips=1):
        """load = SH/LD pin, clock = CLK pin, data = QH pin (all machine.Pin or GPIO numbers).
        clk_inh: optional CLK INH pin; if None it must be tied to GND on the board.
        chips: how many 74HC165s are daisy-chained (QH of the far chip into SER of the near one)."""
        self.ld = load if isinstance(load, Pin) else Pin(load, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.clk = clock if isinstance(clock, Pin) else Pin(clock, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.q = data if isinstance(data, Pin) else Pin(data, Pin.IN)
        self.ld.init(Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.clk.init(Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.inh = None
        if clk_inh is not None:
            self.inh = clk_inh if isinstance(clk_inh, Pin) else Pin(clk_inh, Pin.OUT, value=0)
            self.inh.init(Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.chips = chips

    def read(self):
        """Latch the inputs and shift them in. Returns an int with chips*8 bits:
        for one chip bit 7 = H ... bit 0 = A (1 = that input is high)."""
        self.clk.value(0)
        # Parallel load: SH/LD low, then back high to enter shift mode.
        self.ld.value(0)
        self.ld.value(1)
        if self.inh is not None:
            self.inh.value(0)
        value = 0
        for _ in range(8 * self.chips):
            value = (value << 1) | self.q.value()  # QH already shows the next bit
            self.clk.value(1)  # rising edge shifts the next bit onto QH
            self.clk.value(0)
        return value

    def pin(self, n):
        """Level of input n (0 = A ... 7 = H on the first chip; 8.. = next chip)."""
        v = self.read()
        # Bits of the chip nearest the MCU come out first, so they are the high byte.
        chip = n // 8
        shift = 8 * (self.chips - 1 - chip) + (n % 8)
        return (v >> shift) & 1

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time
from hc165 import HC165

sr = HC165(load={SH_LD}, clock={CLK}, data={QH})
while True:
    b = sr.read()          # bit 7 = H ... bit 0 = A, 1 = input high
    print('IN={:08b}'.format(b))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
